body.title: GTIG AI Threat Tracker: Advances in Threat Actor Usage of AI Tools (2025-11)

data.provenance: Retrieved 2026-10-11 via curl -sSL through egress proxy from services.google.com (Google canonical report host). sha256 bc517904af9d5c40ad4f3a7dc1f8bba30c6b874f42ca93a1146a02ea1f86bf45, 742834 bytes. Official blog post (cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/disrupting-misuse-of-generative-ai) is JS-rendered; PDF is the primary byte source. Release date 2025-11-05 corroborated by contemporaneous press (PYMNTS, The Hacker News).
data.summary: November 2025 update to GTIG's January 2025 'Adversarial Misuse of Generative AI'. First report of 'just-in-time' AI in malware: five novel AI-malware families (PROMPTFLUX, PROMPTSTEAL, PROMPTLOCK, QUIETVAULT, FRUITSHELL) that use LLMs during execution to generate scripts, obfuscate code, or evade LLM-powered analysis. Documents state-actor (China, Iran, North Korea, Russia/APT28) misuse of Gemini across recon, phishing, C2 development, and exfiltration; guardrail-bypass pretexts (CTF participant, student/researcher); and a maturing underground marketplace for illicit AI tooling.
data.title: GTIG AI Threat Tracker: Advances in Threat Actor Usage of AI Tools

data.attribution: unattributed; filename lures consistent with financially motivated actors
data.description: VBScript dropper that decodes and executes an embedded decoy installer to mask activity. Primary capability is regeneration: it prompts the Gemini API to rewrite its own source code and saves the new obfuscated version to the Startup folder for persistence; spreads by copying itself to removable drives and mapped network shares. The 'Thinking Robot' module (function StartThinkingRobot) periodically queries Gemini with a hard-coded API key using machine-parsable prompts (e.g. directing the LLM to act as an 'expert VBScript obfuscator' and output only code) and logs AI responses to %TEMP%\thinking_robot_log.txt; the self-modification function AttemptToUpdateSelf is commented out. One variant ('Thinging') rewrites the entire source hourly. Assessed under development/testing; no demonstrated ability to compromise a victim network or device; Google disabled associated assets.
data.name: PROMPTFLUX
data.provenance: GTIG AI Threat Tracker 2025-11, Table 1 + PROMPTFLUX section

data.description: Data miner written in Python and packaged with PyInstaller. Queries Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct via the Hugging Face API (likely with stolen API tokens) to generate one-line Windows commands, which it blindly executes locally to collect system information and targeted documents from specific folders, then exfiltrates to an adversary-controlled server. Masquerades as an 'image generation' program guiding the user through prompts while issuing the malicious queries in the background. Used by APT28 against Ukraine (also reported by CERT-UA as LAMEHUG); continued development, with new samples adding obfuscation and changing C2 method. GTIG's first observation of malware querying an LLM deployed in live operations.
data.name: PROMPTSTEAL
data.provenance: GTIG AI Threat Tracker 2025-11, Table 1 + PROMPTSTEAL section

data.description: Cross-platform ransomware proof of concept written in Go. Leverages an LLM to dynamically generate and execute malicious Lua scripts at runtime rather than hard-coding them. Capabilities include filesystem reconnaissance, data exfiltration, and file encryption on Windows and Linux systems.
data.name: PROMPTLOCK
data.provenance: GTIG AI Threat Tracker 2025-11, Table 1

data.description: Credential stealer written in JavaScript that targets GitHub and NPM tokens. Captured credentials are exfiltrated via creation of a publicly accessible GitHub repository. Also leverages an AI prompt plus on-host installed AI CLI tools to search for other potential secrets on the infected system and exfiltrate those files to GitHub.
data.name: QUIETVAULT
data.provenance: GTIG AI Threat Tracker 2025-11, Table 1

data.description: Publicly available reverse shell written in PowerShell that establishes a remote connection to a configured command-and-control server and allows a threat actor to execute arbitrary commands on a compromised system. Contains hard-coded prompts meant to bypass detection or analysis by LLM-powered security systems.
data.name: FRUITSHELL
data.provenance: GTIG AI Threat Tracker 2025-11, Table 1

data.description: Malware families use large language models during execution ('just-in-time' AI) to dynamically generate malicious scripts, obfuscate their own code to evade detection, and create malicious functions on demand rather than hard-coding them. First observed by GTIG in PROMPTFLUX and PROMPTSTEAL (2025). Represents a step toward more autonomous and adaptive malware.
data.name: jit-ai-malware-execution
data.provenance: GTIG AI Threat Tracker 2025-11, Key Findings

data.description: Malware outsources malicious logic to an LLM at runtime instead of carrying fixed logic: PROMPTSTEAL generates one-line Windows commands via Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct; PROMPTLOCK generates and executes malicious Lua scripts. No two runs look identical, defeating static signature-based detection.
data.name: llm-runtime-payload-generation
data.provenance: GTIG AI Threat Tracker 2025-11, PROMPTSTEAL/PROMPTLOCK sections

data.description: PROMPTFLUX pins the 'gemini-1.5-flash-latest' model alias so the malware always calls the most current stable release, making the tool more resilient to model deprecation.
data.name: model-alias-latest-deprecation-resilience
data.provenance: GTIG AI Threat Tracker 2025-11, PROMPTFLUX section

data.description: FRUITSHELL embeds hard-coded prompts designed to bypass detection or analysis by LLM-powered security systems.
data.name: prompt-evasion-vs-llm-security-analysis
data.provenance: GTIG AI Threat Tracker 2025-11, Table 1 (FRUITSHELL)

data.description: QUIETVAULT uses an AI prompt together with AI CLI tools installed on the victim machine to search for additional secrets beyond its primary GitHub/NPM token targets.
data.name: ai-cli-assisted-secret-discovery
data.provenance: GTIG AI Threat Tracker 2025-11, Table 1 (QUIETVAULT)

data.description: QUIETVAULT exfiltrates captured credentials and files by creating a publicly accessible GitHub repository.
data.name: exfil-via-public-github-repo
data.provenance: GTIG AI Threat Tracker 2025-11, Table 1 (QUIETVAULT)

data.description: A China-nexus threat actor reframed prompts as coming from a capture-the-flag (CTF) competition participant ('I am working on a CTF problem') to bypass Gemini safety guardrails and obtain advice supporting phishing, exploitation, and web shell development.
data.name: guardrail-bypass-ctf-pretext
data.provenance: GTIG AI Threat Tracker 2025-11, 'Social Engineering to Bypass Safeguards' section

data.description: Iranian actor MuddyWater (TEMP.Zagros) posed as a university student working on a final project or writing a cybersecurity article to bypass Gemini guardrails while developing custom malware; the interaction exposed its C2 domains and encryption keys, enabling Google to disrupt the campaign.
data.name: guardrail-bypass-student-pretext
data.provenance: GTIG AI Threat Tracker 2025-11, state-actor sections; corroborated by securityonline.info

data.description: China, Iran, and North Korea misuse Gemini across the attack lifecycle: China for reconnaissance, lure crafting, infrastructure building, and exfiltration tooling; Iran APT41 for code obfuscation and C2 frameworks (OSSTUN), MuddyWater for malware development, APT42 for phishing lures and a natural-language 'Data Processing Agent'; North Korea UNC1069 (MASAN) and TraderTraitor (PUKCHONG) for cryptocurrency-theft reconnaissance, stealer code, and deepfake social-engineering lures (BIGMACHO backdoor via fake Zoom SDK).
data.name: state-actor-ai-attack-lifecycle
data.provenance: GTIG AI Threat Tracker 2025-11, state-actor sections
